known_gaps: Appendix D of D1 — the per-permit process maps and written summaries, including the DPH Certificate of Sanitation map — is not in the extracted text (the .txt ends at p. 20, the appendix cover page). The richest sequencing artifact in the gold document is therefore unread; so is Figure 1, the end-to-end cross-department map on p. 5.

The 'Permit application timelines' bar chart on p. 8 (average and longest time per permit, including DPH Food Permit to Operate) is an image; no numeric values survive in the extracted text. This is the one place a DPH-specific duration may exist.
The DPH plan review fee amount is not captured: the food plan review fee schedule linked from D3 was not fetched in Wave 1. Fee error cannot be scored for SF.

SF's placard categories / score bands are not confirmed from a primary source. The 'Restaurant health inspection posters and what they mean' page 404'd on fetch (saved as sf_gov_placards.txt, a Not Found page) and the data.sf.gov LIVES dataset page is JS-rendered.

No measured DPH plan-check or permit-issuance turnaround exists in any source. The 20-business-day figure in HSC 114380 is a statutory ceiling; D1's own Recommendation 1 exists because the measurement does not.

Mobile food facilities are out of this model's scope (SF runs a separate 5-classification MFF track with public-right-of-way vs. private-property branches; see sf_gov_mobile_guide.txt and sf_gov_food_truck_guide.txt). A separate gold model would be needed.

The declared SF.gov pages were fetched as HTML-to-text with the site navigation repeated four times before the body; quotes here were taken from the body after the last 'Find contacts' marker. A solver reading the raw .txt sees the same content but must strip the chrome.

Sibling-process contamination risk for scoring: the SF food permit sits next to the DBI building permit, the SFFD Place of Assembly permit, and the ABC liquor license. A29 is included as a labelled boundary case.
notes: Why this is the gold for SF: the 2015 Controller/CSA memo is the only public document that states the DPH food permit is gated on two other departments' sign-off. Nothing on sf.gov says this. The whole applicant-facing footprint presents the health permit as a single-department deliverable with a 1-month (D2) or 6-8-week (D4) lead time — a contradiction between two live city pages that is itself a scoring target. Six activities (A19-A24) are staff_only and all six come from D1 alone: the SFFD and Planning referrals, the hold state, consolidated billing, the withheld-permit failure mode, and the EHD system of record. Structural note for cross-county comparison: SF folds DPH plan review *inside* the DBI single-Permit-Center submittal as a routing station (A08/A09), whereas LA County and San Diego County take EH plan check as a direct, separate submittal to the health department. gold_tier is 'designed+observed' because the process model is designed-tier while two timing figures are records-derived: the DBI FY04-14 permit-duration analysis (Appendix B, observed but not restaurant-specific) and the applicant survey (n=15, self-reported). Reported per-tier scores should treat the process model as designed-only.
